notes: Account background: mid-market product analytics company that overlays in-app guidance and contextual chat for customers. Heavy usage on chat + embeddings for search and reranking.
Current provider: OpenAI (gpt-4o / embeddings) for prod; exploring vendor lock-in + cost predictability -> Redwood evaluation.
Primary goal: move from Hosted (fast onboarding) -> Dedicated (predictable throughput) within 6 months if POC satisfactory.
POC scope: parity for existing prompts, basic streaming parity, embedding similarity within +/- 2% on evaluation set, and end-to-end latency under 200ms p95 for single-turn chat.
Key quote from CTO (J. Alvarez): 'We need drop-in parity for hundreds of prompts; regressions are the real blocker, not raw p50 latency.'
Technical concerns called out on calls:
- prompt-parity: tokenization differences and default stop sequences causing truncation on 3 prompts
- streaming behavior: chunk sizes and timing affect front-end UX; want to see identical initial token latencies
- embeddings parity: ANN index recall must be within 1-2% of current baseline
POC implementation notes:
- Started by proxying a small traffic slice (5% of sessions) to Redwood Hosted; instrumentation includes trace ids and token-level timing
- Built a thin compatibility shim to translate incumbent API calls to Redwood SDK; shim repo: github.com/meadowridge/poc-redwood-shim (internal)
- Run eval harness nightly (1000 prompt pairs) — results stored in shared Drive (see linked_drive_docs)
POC findings so far:
- Latency: p50=72ms, p95=188ms on Hosted (eu-west region tests), meets target but tail close to limit
- Cost: estimated monthly token spend would be ~1.8x with current setup on Hosted; Dedicated sizing conversation to reduce unit costs
- Regressions: 7/1000 prompts flagged as 'semantic drift' vs incumbent; most are prompt-formatting sensitive (stop tokens, temperature differences).
- Embeddings: cosine similarity median 0.985 vs incumbent; a few outliers on short notes -> flagged for retraining prompt templates
Migration plan discussed:
- Phase 1 (Hosted pilot): validate parity, run canary for 2 weeks, gather regression metrics
- Phase 2 (Dedicated POC): baseline dedicated configuration for steady-state throughput, negotiate commit levels
- Phase 3 (Cutover): split traffic, roll back policy to incumbent if regression spike > threshold
Operational asks from Meadowridge:
- per-route dashboards (token-level cost + latency), automatic regression alerts tied to nightly evals,
- SSO + audit logs + KMS integration before Dedicated go-live,
- SLA: 99.9% uptime and p95 latency guarantees they can present to their customers
Sales/Commercial notes:
- Meadowridge is price-sensitive; finance wants options: committed Dedicated with burst credits OR hybrid routing (hosted for bursts).
- Request: conservative pricing sheet for 100k-500k tokens/day and a scenario with 2x traffic growth (Drive: pricing deck link).
Action items from last call (03/10):
- SE (Ravi) to deliver regression report with examples and suggested prompt fixes by 2026-03-14 (INF-1102),
- Commercial (Ava) to produce two offer variants (12-month commit, 24-month commit + lite-support) by 2026-03-17,
- Legal to kick off SOC2 appendix / DPA review; Meadowridge to share vendor DPA template
Open blockers (detail):
- Prompt-parity: needs deterministic mapping for stop tokens and temperature defaults; engineering has spike to propose shim adjustments
- Regression detection: want tie-in from Redwood Optimize to nightly evals and automated rollback triggers — asked for product roadmapping note
- Dedicated pricing: internal procurement requires a mid-range ARR estimate for exec approval (we provided 80k-250k ballpark)
Meeting artifacts: Fireflies transcripts and timestamps attached (see linked_fireflies).
Tone/relationship: technical, collaborative; Meadowridge is pragmatic — willing to trade higher initial hosted costs for a predictable Dedicated commitment that halves unit costs.
notes_summary: Mid-market SaaS evaluating Redwood Hosted -> Dedicated. POC shows promising latency and embeddings parity but several prompt-regression cases. Next steps: regression report, pricing variants, SOC2/DPA. Main blockers: prompt parity, tail latency SLA, committed pricing.
